source_locators: Six tall-grass prairie paddocks in Oklahoma were rotationally grazed for ten years at 12.5, 25 or 50 cows per hectare; two adjacent ungrazed sites were controls.
Penetration resistance and bulk density increased in the upper 10 centimetres, with significant impact in the high-density treatment.
Surface infiltration fell from 28.5 centimetres per day in ungrazed controls to 7, 5 and 5 centimetres per day under low, moderate and high stocking density.
The field experiment compared soil compaction caused by cattle trampling and tractor use with uncompacted grassland and evaluated grass yield and quality.
First-cut grass-silage yield loss reached 19.0 percent under cattle trampling; the larger 37.7-percent tractor result is excluded.
By the third year, the experiment measured a 14.3-percent annual loss of grass dry-matter yield.

transformations.formula: Compute (28.5 - 5) / 28.5 × 100 = 82.456140 percent loss using the ungrazed-control and high-density-treatment infiltration endpoints.
Normalize the source-reported maximum 19-percent first-cut grass-silage yield loss from cattle trampling; exclude the 37.7-percent tractor-compaction result.
Normalize ten treatment years and six grazed USDA paddocks; retain two adjacent ungrazed sites as control design rather than additional affected extent.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: The USDA experiment measures a specific Oklahoma tall-grass prairie system after ten years and the SRUC/AHDB result is a separate grassland trial; neither represents global pasture prevalence. Infiltration change is calculated from source-reported endpoints and is not converted to runoff, erosion or plant-available water volume. The 19-percent yield loss is a maximum first-cut result; tractor compaction and the year-three 14.3-percent annual dry-matter result remain unscored corroboration. Soil texture, moisture, grazing rotation and recovery can materially change outcomes.
receipts.freshness: Historical ten-year USDA grazing experiment plus current SRUC/AHDB research summary reviewed 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: Controlled field evidence directly measures cattle stocking density, soil penetration and bulk-density response, infiltration loss, treatment duration and cattle-specific grass-yield burden.
higher_priority_failures: The evidence consists of bounded Oklahoma and Scottish/UK experiments rather than a current global grazing-compaction observation.
No comparable global monthly or annual soil-compaction series meets the current-data coverage and historical-distribution gates.
